description:
Newly VISIBLE in s468bc (the file used to refuse at transpile; #1037).

`t/class/utf8.t` line 18 is `STDOUT->binmode( ":encoding(UTF-8)" );` and PCL
answers `Can't locate object method "binmode" via package "STDOUT" (perhaps
you forgot to load "STDOUT"?)`.  perl treats a bareword filehandle in a method
slot as an IO::Handle object, so the whole IO::Handle / IO::File method set
(`binmode`, `autoflush`, `print`, `say`, `printf`, `close`, `eof`, `fileno`,
`opened`, `blocking`, ...) is callable that way, on the bareword handles and
on lexical ones alike.

PCL already has every one of these as a BUILTIN with a handle slot (the
`%p-fh-arg` family, #1032).  The missing piece is the METHOD route: a method
call whose invocant names a filehandle (a bareword handle, a glob, or a box
holding one) should dispatch to the builtin.  That is a generic mechanism, not
a module fact -- CLAUDE.md 9a -- so it belongs beside the existing handle-slot
contract in the runtime, or as an `IO::Handle` shim in lib/ whose methods call
the builtins.  Decide which by asking whether user code can write it in plain
Perl: it can (`sub binmode { my $fh = shift; CORE::binmode($fh, @_) }`), so
the shim is the default answer and the parser/runtime job is only to make a
bareword invocant resolve to the handle.

Not urgent on its own: `t/class/utf8.t` would die two statements later at its
`class` block anyway, which is why the file keeps its class registration.  It
is filed because the shape is common in real code.

=== DONE (s473f) ===
FIXED, at the layer the task named.  THE RUNTIME'S JOB IS ONLY TO SAY THAT A
HANDLE HAS A CLASS; the methods stay perl, in lib/IO/Handle.pm and lib/IO.pm.
Two hooks, each where it costs nothing: %pcl-invocant-class (a box holding a
stream/socket, or a typeglob, with no class of its own) and p-method-call (a
NAME that names an OPEN handle -- asked ONLY once the class package is known
not to exist, so an ordinary class method never pays).  perl names the class
IO::File; PCL uses IO::Handle, so only a "Can't locate object method" message
differs.  A class of one's own WINS (probed on a blessed object with its own
`print`).  perl goes one step further -- its handle wins even over a package of
that NAME that exists -- and PCL prefers the package; noted at the site.

TWO REAL BUGS UNDER IT, both found by running the shim:
  * %p-binmode-impl compared external formats with EQ.  The byte format is a
    LIST and SBCL hands back an EQUAL copy, never the same object (measured),
    so "already in that discipline" NEVER fired and `binmode($fh)` on a handle
    that was already bytes took the REBUILD path, which dups the descriptor and
    CLOSES the original: `my $g = $fh; binmode($g); print {$fh} "hello"` wrote
    NOTHING (identical on the base -- pre-existing, a silent data loss).
  * the shim's `binmode` dereferenced ($$fh), core's way of getting the glob
    out of a blessed glob ref, which names nothing under PCL's handle model.
    lib/IO/Handle.pm's third documented difference from core.
And p-aref-unbox-elem / %p-hash-unbox-elem now keep the BOX for a handle
payload, as they already do for every other reference kind.

Guard Pl/t/handle-place-01.t rows 127-155.  Commit 96dd8785.
subject: `STDOUT->binmode(...)` dies: no IO::Handle methods on a bareword filehandle
